REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JUNE 13, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made during regular business hours by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and the document(s) will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  None.

 Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during

  Regional Park for placement of additional pickleball courts in the City.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to authorize administrative-initiated

  2023-26/CSA 2023-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget Preparation Policy
  (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  Account/Project: 110-364-61340 Water Operations Outside Services
  Amount: $61,000 (Transfer)
  Justification: On March 14, 2024, emergency repairs and the removal of an abandoned
  two-inch water service were required due to a leak at 18230 Elgers Street. Additional
  funding is necessary to pay the City's on-call contractor for these essential services. This
  amendment proposes transferring $61,000 from account 110-363-67020 (Water Production
  and Distribution MWD Purchase) to cover the costs of the repairs and removal;

  Account/Project: cp17199 Groundwater Remediation Project
  Amount: $108,000
  Justification: As part of the Groundwater Remediation Project, an amendment is needed
  to cover fees due to the California Water Boards. These fees are for the discharge of water
  containing arsenic to the storm drain system; and

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public

  3. Award a contract to F.M. Thomas Air Conditioning Inc., in the amount of $1,134,892,
  for Swim/Fitness Center rehabilitation boiler replacement, Project No. 20201;

  4. Award a contract to IDS Group, in the amount of $5,500, for construction

  replacement, Project No. 20201; and

  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Acting Finance Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  This item was received and filed and there was no further action taken.

9B.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Fine Arts and Historical Commission, on a vote of 4-1,
  to approve the following:

  Review and consideration of a concept for the commission of a sculpture to be included as
  part of the City’s Art in Public Places Program. The sculpture is generally described as the
  Cerritos Cow and is proposed to commemorate the City’s dairy farming heritage
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Sam Desai expressed support for Council communication with City advisory board members
  related to suggested program direction.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  Manager or designee to negotiate a contract with the National Sculptors' Guild for the
  purchase of the “Milking Time” sculpture by Jane DeDecker, proceed with the
  development of plans for the location of the sculpture with Council-suggested
  amendments (to modify the cow head placement, incorporate a dog in the place of a
  cat, incorporate a Dairy Valley logo placed on the feed bag, and for the sculpture to
  accurately reflect the appropriate time period), and to obtain cost estimates for the
  shipping, installation and associated landscaping/hardscaping required to complete the
  project; and

  2. Direct staff to provide the City Council with a report for final review and consideration of
  the contract, final sculpture design, proposed locations, associated landscape/hardscape
  improvements and additional costs associated with the completion of the project
  (COUNCIL).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Catherine Pascual expressed support for extending Advisory Board, Commission, and
  Committee Member terms through the next election date.

  Sam Desai expressed concern regarding community involvement in Advisory Board,
  Commissions, and Committees, and expressed support for extending member terms
  through the next election date.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to approve an additional 90-day

  allowing for the current terms to extend for a total period not more than 180 days, if
  necessary (through October 27, 2024), by waiving full reading of and introducing
